name: 26-projection-verdict-no-way-down
incident: 2026-08-21 - cam-schuppen, morning: 'day mode would read ... staying night' every 26 seconds, reference never came down
description:
Scenario 23's defect, reopened through the OTHER night verdict. 23 taught the r >= ir_ratio_night branch to lower the reference when a silent probe answers night below the probe bar. The filter-cost projection branch ('the room supplies the light, but day mode would bounce off night_gain') is ALSO a night verdict, and it forgot the same lesson: it resets the trigger hold but leaves the reference standing, so on a scene resting below the bar the jump trigger re-arms and fires again every probe_confirm_s, indefinitely. Measured on a shed camera at 08:39: probe pairs 26 s apart, each dimming the image for the 8 s settle, reference 5753 over a scene reading 1040 - verdict correct every time, cadence unbounded.

Phase 1 (t<600) reproduces how the camera got there, straight from its own morning log: r=1.52 sends it to day, day mode reads 5.61x the night level, the absolute rule reverts it and learns the cost. Phase 2 (t=600): the shed brightens to 1040 - far below the re-anchored bar, but 1040 * 5.61 is still above night_gain, so day mode is genuinely not viable. The projection verdict must now lower the reference like any other proven night-below-the-bar, after which the trigger stays quiet until the scene genuinely halves again. The old code fails the probe budget by an order of magnitude.

expect_log: day mode reads 5\.[456][0-9]x the night level
